references.text: The repentant thief asked Jesus to remember him when He came into His kingdom ([ref:Luk 23:42|Luke 23:42]). Jesus' answer in verse 43 is the direct response to this prayer, where He promises him a place in paradise.

Paul refers to paradise as a heavenly place he was caught up to ([ref:2 Kor 12:4|2 Corinthians 12:4]). The term "paradis" (παράδεισος) is used here just as in Jesus' promise to the thief, pointing to God's heavenly presence.

Jesus promises the one who overcomes that they will eat from the tree of life in God's paradise ([ref:Åp 2:7|Revelation 2:7]). This links paradise with final salvation and eternal existence with God, just as Jesus promised the repentant thief.

Paradise (the garden in Eden) is first mentioned in Scripture ([ref:1 Mos 2:8-9|Genesis 2:8-9]). The word παράδεισος is used in the Septuagint for the Garden of Eden, and Jesus' promise of paradise points back to the original fellowship between God and humanity.

Jesus says there are many rooms in His Father's house, and that He goes to prepare a place for His disciples ([ref:Joh 14:2-3|John 14:2-3]). The promise to the thief to be with Jesus in paradise "today" reflects this promise of being taken to the Father's dwelling.

Paul expresses his desire to depart and be with Christ, which is far better ([ref:Fil 1:23|Philippians 1:23]). This confirms that being with Christ after death is a real and immediate reality, just as Jesus promised the thief.

Salvation is by grace through faith, not by works ([ref:Ef 2:8-9|Ephesians 2:8-9]). The repentant thief had no opportunity to do good works, yet was saved by faith alone—a strong example of the gospel of grace that Jesus preached.

Isaiah speaks of the righteous who dies and enters into peace ([ref:Jes 57:1-2|Isaiah 57:1-2]). Jesus' words to the thief fulfill this promise that the believer goes directly into rest and peace with God.

In the parable of the rich man and Lazarus, Lazarus is carried by angels to Abraham's bosom after death ([ref:Luk 16:22-23|Luke 16:22-23]). This illustrates the concept of immediate life after death in fellowship with the righteous, parallel to Jesus' promise of paradise "today".

Stephen prayed in his final moments: "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit" ([ref:Apg 7:59|Acts 7:59]). Stephen expected, just like the thief on the cross, to come immediately into Jesus' presence after death.
